question: Which Nigerian federal body is primarily responsible for setting national environmental protection laws regarding waste?

options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control

explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment takes the lead in creating national policies and rules to protect the environment from hazardous waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why is proper health care waste management strictly regulated in clinical settings?

options.A: To ensure the facility uses less electricity every month
options.B: To make hospital compounds look neat for visiting inspectors
options.C: To prevent the spread of infections and protect community health
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing office supplies

explanation: Strict rules are necessary because improperly managed medical waste can transmit dangerous diseases to staff, patients, and the public. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which of the following is classified as pathological waste?

options.A: Used office paper and empty cardboard boxes
options.C: Recognizable human tissues and body parts

explanation: Pathological waste specifically refers to body parts, tissues, and organs removed during surgeries or autopsies. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: A nurse discards an empty glass drug ampoule. Which waste category does this item belong to?
explanation: Even though ampoules are glass rather than needles, their sharp edges can easily cut skin, so they must be treated as sharps waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: At what point should health care waste be segregated?

options.A: After the cleaning staff transport it outside
options.B: At the exact point and time of generation
options.C: Only when the waste bins are completely full

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately where the waste is produced to prevent mixing hazardous and non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: What is the primary danger of filling a waste collection bag to the absolute brim?

options.A: It violates local tax laws regarding commercial building capacity
options.B: It automatically changes the chemical composition of the waste inside
options.C: It increases the risk of spills, tears, and accidental injuries during handling
options.D: It makes the waste lighter and harder for handlers to grip

explanation: Overfilled bags are difficult to tie securely and prone to bursting or puncturing, exposing staff to injury. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which feature is essential for a central health care waste storage room?

options.B: Large glass windows for direct sunlight exposure
options.C: Open access for patients and visitors
options.D: Secure locks to prevent unauthorized entry

explanation: Central storage areas must be locked securely to keep unauthorized persons, scavengers, and animals away from hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: Why must internal transport routes avoid patient dining areas and crowded waiting rooms?

options.A: To minimize the risk of accidental exposure and public anxiety
options.B: To prevent the waste from cooling down too quickly
options.C: To ensure the waste carts move at a faster speed
options.D: To comply with architectural design rules for elevators

explanation: Moving hazardous waste through clean, crowded public spaces creates unnecessary infection risks and alarms patients. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: What is the primary mechanism of an autoclave in waste treatment?

options.A: Dissolving metal instruments in strong acids
options.B: Burning waste at extremely high open flames
options.C: Freezing biological specimens to sub-zero temperatures

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to kill all infectious agents present in medical waste effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why is encapsulation often used specifically for pharmaceutical waste?

options.A: To turn expired tablets into sweet-tasting liquid syrups
options.B: To immobilize chemical drugs and prevent them from entering water supplies
options.C: To bleach colored medicine bottles so they can be recycled
options.D: To make heavy metal containers easier to burn in an incinerator

explanation: Encapsulation binds drugs in a solid matrix like cement, stopping them from dissolving and leaching into soil and groundwater. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the tiny puncture wound tightly with adhesive tape
options.B: Wash the site immediately with soap and running water
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow joint

explanation: Immediate washing helps remove and flush out infectious pathogens before they can establish an infection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: What does the concept of universal precautions mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Using disposable plastic syringes only once per hospital
options.B: Testing every single admitted patient for rare tropical diseases
options.C: Treating all blood and body fluids as if they are infectious
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for every routine physical exam

explanation: Universal precautions assume every patient's fluids carry blood-borne pathogens, ensuring staff use protection consistently. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: A nurse walks into a ward and finds a junior colleague throwing a used syringe into a regular black polythene bag. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Correct the colleague immediately and ensure the syringe is moved to the sharps box
options.B: Ignore the mistake because cleaners will sort it out later anyway
options.C: Write an official query letter to the hospital medical director
options.D: Remove all waste bins from the ward to teach everyone a lesson

explanation: Nurses have a duty to correct segregation errors instantly to maintain a safe working and clinical environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: Why is nurse-led education for patients and visitors important for waste management?

options.A: To train family members how to incinerate trash in the hospital yard
options.B: To encourage visitors to bring their own waste bags from home
options.C: To prevent visitors from accidentally touching hazardous waste or opening bins
options.D: To reduce the hospital budget spent on buying cleaning detergents

explanation: Visitors often do not know clinical waste risks, so nursing guidance keeps them from touching contaminated materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)
